notes.1a: This part was very well answered with most candidates accurately finding the Maclaurin’s series, ( ) though a few accepted a zero value of f'' 0 without checking their work.
notes.1b: Almost all candidates substituted the correct expansion from (a) which led to the required approximation.
notes.2a: Almost all candidates knew how to approach this question and completed it to a high standard. There was some inaccuracy when solving linear equations to find the particular integral and some problems with notation. A few candidates gave expressions instead of equations as their answer.
notes.2b: Most candidates successfully stated an approximate solution using their answer to (a).
notes.3a: The majority of candidates calculated the determinant accurately to show that the system of equations does not have a unique solution. A few candidates accepted a non-zero determinant without checking their work.
notes.3b: Most candidates were able to show that the system is consistent by manipulating the equations. The strongest candidates also gave a complete and correct geometric description.
notes.3c: – (d) Most candidates were able to derive a contradiction by manipulating equations. The strongest candidates also gave a complete and correct geometric description.
notes.4a: Strong candidates formed a correct expression for the sum of the areas of the rectangles and applied the standard result for the sum of cubes to accurately derive the given result.
notes.4b: Strong candidates adapted their solution to (a) and derived a suitable lower bound.
notes.5a: Most candidates differentiated cos–1t correctly using implicit differentiation.
notes.5b: The majority of candidates found the first derivative correctly using parametric differentiation. The attempts to find the second derivative varied in length, with stronger candidates showing the required level of algebraic fluency and remembering to divide by after differentiating with respect to t.
notes.6a: After expanding ( z−z−1)4 using the binomial expansion, stronger candidates grouped together terms clearly before applying the identity zn +z−n =2cosnθto justify fully the given result. Alternatively, a few candidates applied cos2θ+sin2θ=1, and were usually successful too.
notes.6b: Most candidates found the integrating factor correctly and, after multiplying both sides of the equation by sinθ, were able to apply the result given in (a). Stronger candidates maintained accuracy throughout, particularly when substituting in the initial conditions.
notes.7a: Most candidates found the first part of this question straightforward. A few candidates spent time finding det ( P−λI ) instead of reading directly from the diagonal of the matrix.
notes.7b: Stronger candidates were able to maintain accuracy throughout their solution, both when manipulating the characteristic equation and when substituting in for P and P2.
notes.7c: Most candidates applied A=PDP–1 using their answer to (b). A few candidates took the lengthy approach of finding P–1 again without using the characteristic equation.
notes.8a: Most sketches were accurate, showing asymptotes x =0 and y =1. A few candidates unnecessarily sketched the curve for x<0.
notes.8b: This part of the question was answered well with the majority of candidates accurately substituting coth and cosech in terms of exponentials and combining using a common denominator.
notes.8c: Stronger candidates clearly applied the chain rule and required double angle formula to justify the given derivative.
notes.8d: Most candidates accurately recalled the formula for arc length and applied the results given in (b) and (c) to reach the given answer. Finding the logarithmic form of cosh–12 was not problematic for most candidates.
notes.key_messages:
• Candidates should show all the steps in their solutions, particularly when proving a given result.
• Candidates should read questions carefully so that they answer all aspects in adequate depth,
particularly when a geometric interpretation is required.
• Candidates should make use of results derived or given in earlier parts of a question.
notes.general_comments:
The majority of candidates demonstrated very good knowledge across the whole syllabus. They showed
their working clearly and were accurate in their handling of algebra and calculus. They also showed
understanding of linear algebra. There was no evidence that candidates were short of time. Sometimes
candidates did not fully support their answers and reached a conclusion without justification, particularly
where answers were given within the question. There were many scripts of a high standard.
